title: Sharp Critical Minimax Laws and No-Learning Thresholds in Continuous-Time Adaptive Control
summary: We study episodic continuous-time control with an unknown vector control gain, scalar state, quadratic action cost, and smooth convex terminal cost. In the scalar Gaussian experiment, let $Δ(H)$ denote the minimax improvement over zero control and set $δ=\sqrt2H^2-1$. We prove the critical law $$ Δ(H)\asymp δ^4\sqrt{\log(1/δ)} \qquad (δ\downarrow0), $$ with a matching lower and upper bound. The lower bound follows from a uniform deficit--energy inequality valid for fully adaptive controls with unbounded amplitudes, while a moving soft-threshold feedback attains the rate.
